clue.text: Record poem about island event

indicators.note: the record and poem together go about, or around, the island's letters

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A poet records a reading about an island, and the release becomes quite an occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an occurrence or incident in a series is one in a sequence of happenings.

clue.text: Nationalist conveniently hosts group

indicators.note: hosts means holds within, so the group goes inside

parts.note: pat, as an adverb, means conveniently or at just the right moment
a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: A nationalist happens to be entertaining a band of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a patriot is someone who fervently supports their nation.

clue.text: Flyer in posh part of London paper

parts.note: SW1 is the smart London postcode covering Westminster and Belgravia, with 1 read as I
the FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A pilot appears in a newspaper from an upmarket London district.
explanation.walkthrough: SW1 is a London postcode around Westminster and Belgravia; the digit 1 becomes I.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a swift is a fast bird that spends most of its life on the wing.

clue.text: Daughter spoke out about tense workstation

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about the tense letter
out means the letters of spoke are put out of order

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A daughter spoke up about stress in the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ESKOP (the anagram of SPOKE, from 'out') around T.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer for use at a desk is a work station, as opposed to a laptop.

clue.text: First person to settle in South Sea archipelago

indicators.note: the South letter goes in among the letters of the first person and the settling verb

parts.note: I is the first-person pronoun
lands, as a bird lands, means comes down to settle
S is the compass abbreviation for South

explanation.surface: The first explorer to make a home in a Pacific island chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South Sea' looks like part of the definition, but only 'South' is wordplay and 'Sea' merely dresses the archipelago.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an archipelago is a group or chain of many isles.

clue.text: Girl associated with stars briefly

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: stellar means relating to stars

explanation.surface: A young woman linked for a short time to celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Stella is a woman's first name, from the Latin for star.

clue.text: Right-angled triangle has one next to it

definitions.meaning: the hypotenuse is a single lengthy edge of such a triangle

explanation.surface: A geometry fact followed by a placement direction.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as three words for the first sense: the hypotenuse is a lengthy edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: beside or adjacent, positioned next to something.

clue.text: Journalist goes up to present warrant

indicators.note: in a down clue, goes up means the word is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
to serve is to present food or a ball

explanation.surface: A reporter climbs up to hand over an arrest warrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to warrant something is to merit or earn it.

clue.text: Cynic ruffled top Irishman, Patrick perhaps

indicators.note: ruffled means disturbed, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: St Patrick is a saint, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: A sour man upset a leading Irishman, maybe called Patrick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patrick perhaps' looks like the Irishman's name but gives ST, a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who distrusts and dislikes humankind is a cynic about people.

clue.text: Personal repair kit on display in the Tuileries

indicators.note: the letters are on view inside the words the Tuileries, spanning their join

explanation.surface: A sewing kit seen in a Paris garden, perhaps in a shop or exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles and thread, used for mending on the go.

clue.text: Rent hotel or school in south-east Clydesdale, for one

indicators.note: the preceding pieces sit inside the south-east letters

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east
to hire is to rent
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Advice to let out a hotel or school somewhere in the south-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clydesdale' looks like a Scottish place; here it is the breed of heavy draught horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Clydesdale is a heavy draught breed, a type of big farm horse like the Shire.

clue.text: Order fool to withdraw article in Times

indicators.note: withdrawing, in a down-to-up sense of pulling back, means the word for fool is read backwards

parts.note: to kid someone is to fool them

indicators.note: the article is placed inside the two time letters

parts.note: T is a symbol for times, as in a multiplication sign, so two of them
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A fool is ordered to retract a newspaper article in The Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a diktat is an order or decree imposed without consultation.

clue.text: Utterly base and gruesome moral tale

parts.note: all, as in all alone, means utterly
e is the base of natural logarithms
gory means gruesome and bloody

explanation.surface: A moral fable dismissed as thoroughly low and grisly.
explanation.walkthrough: E for 'base' is the mathematical constant, the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an allegory is a story with a hidden moral or political meaning, such as a fable.

clue.text: North-west town's lost rare items in soup kitchen

indicators.note: the town has lost a letter, meaning the rare letter is dropped

parts.note: Stockport is a town in north-west England, near Manchester; the 's gives the final S

explanation.surface: A northern English town has mislaid some rare objects from its soup kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: STOCKPORT is a town in Greater Manchester, north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: big pots for simmering broth are standard equipment where soup is made for the needy.

clue.text: Minister nearly left Germany devastated

parts.note: C is short for circa, meaning about or nearly

indicators.note: devastated means wrecked, so the country's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A government minister almost left a war-torn Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks political; here it is a church minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a minister of religion is a cleric.

clue.text: Snide remarks set back great art in Paris

indicators.note: set back means the word for great is reversed

parts.note: big means great
in French, tu es means thou art

explanation.surface: Sneering comments put back the cause of fine art in the French capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: jibes or taunts are mocking, snide remarks.

clue.text: Present side at Old Trafford starts to earn respect

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field; Old Trafford is a Manchester cricket ground

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A team at Manchester's ground offers a gift to win respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' looks like a team, but it is the off side of a cricket field; Old Trafford is a Test cricket ground as well as a football one.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to offer is to present something for acceptance.

clue.text: Lock worker's increase in scale

indicators.note: the increase sits in the scale word

parts.note: fur is the scaly limescale deposit inside a kettle
a rise is an increase

explanation.surface: A locksmith's pay rise is set according to a scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door or canal, but it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdresser, in French terms, is a worker who styles locks of hair.

clue.text: Endless urban street party growing in volume

indicators.note: endless means the word for street loses its final letter

parts.note: a crescent is a curved street of houses in a town
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A street party in town that never ends and gets louder and louder.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical term: a crescendo is a gradual increase in loudness.

clue.text: He abandons charities in trouble, taking off

indicators.note: in trouble means disordered, so the letters of charities are mixed, minus those abandoned

parts.note: the word He, given as written, is the part that abandons the mix

explanation.surface: A man walks away from struggling charities and leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' says HE comes out of CHARITIES; the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking by imitation, as a parody takes off its target, is satirical.

clue.text: Dope turns up all right in bust

indicators.note: the reversed word and right go in the failure word

parts.note: a dud is a failure or bust

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means the word all is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: Drugs show up, fine, during a police raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' and 'bust' suggest drugs and a raid; here dope is a fool and bust a dud.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a dope is a stupid person, a dimwit.

clue.text: How come bar's cutting noise from 11?

indicators.note: the bar word cuts into the question word

parts.note: how come means why
an inn is a pub with a bar

explanation.surface: Wondering why a pub interrupts with a horse's neigh.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is SHIRE HORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-pitched neigh is a sound a horse makes.

clue.text: Fellow feeling round government office for ruler

indicators.note: the fellow-feeling word goes round the government letter

parts.note: kinship is a feeling of fellowship and affinity

explanation.surface: A sense of camaraderie surrounds a government department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Government office' reads as one phrase, but 'office' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The position or dignity of a monarch is the office held by a ruler.

clue.text: Church office worker lied regularly

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of lied

explanation.surface: A clerk at a church office told lies on a routine basis.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a temple is a place of worship, a church or shrine.

clue.text: Fly plane over Germany and Spain

indicators.note: the plane is over, covering, the Germany letter

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter aircraft
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Take an aircraft above Germany and Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like a verb but is the noun, an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a midge is a tiny biting gnat, a type of insect.

clue.text: Preacher's small sin involving suspect monies

indicators.note: the sin word involves, or contains, the shuffled money letters

parts.note: to err is to sin

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so these letters are not in their honest order

explanation.surface: A clergyman's minor failing involves dodgy money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preacher's' hides the link: the 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A person given to delivering sermons, often tediously, is a kind of preacher.

clue.text: 15 characters in Pride and Prejudice

indicators.note: the letters are characters inside the words Pride and, a pun on characters in a novel

explanation.surface: Clergymen who appear as people in Jane Austen's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' suggests people in the novel, but means letters; 15 is CLERGYMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a dean is a senior cleric heading a cathedral chapter, so a type of minister.

clue.text: Golden reefs flanking northern 5

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: the reefs word flanks, or sits either side of, the northern letter

parts.note: keys or cays are low islands or reefs

explanation.surface: Gilded reefs on either side of a northern group of islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 is ISLANDS; the Orkneys are an island group off the north coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Orkney islands form an archipelago off northern Scotland.

clue.text: Pages and pages of articles of faith on board

indicators.note: being on a vessel means being inside it, so the faith word goes within

parts.note: a board here is the steamship one boards, abbreviated as two letters for steamship
a creed is a religious faith or set of beliefs

explanation.surface: Long texts of religious belief carried aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is the crossword convention for going inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: screeds are long, often tedious pieces of writing running to many pages.
